What's your best story from when you were a kid?

I already posted my favorite in /v/stories but I'll copy/paste it here.

Like any parent, my mother took me shopping with her.

Pretty normal stuff. Being about 3 or 4 years old, I was not particularly skilled in the way of social interaction or personal boundaries. As you can imagine, that led to me saying some things that would have best been left unsaid.

I was sitting in the of the shopping cart while in the checkout line. There was a large, tan man checking out his things in front of us. When he turned to put his stuff on the conveyor belt, I got a full look at him. He was "round," fairly dark, wore flowery swim trunks, and a tank top. He also had a bandanna on his head and an eyepatch.

Young me was entranced. This was completely outlandish to me; I hadn't seen a pirate in a supermarket before!

"Stop staring," said my mother, quietly.

I did not stop.

"Stop staring!" she said, more sternly.

I couldn't help myself. I wanted to talk to him in a way he'd understand. I looked at him right in the eye.

"Arr, matey!" I blurted.

My mom gasped, but the man just let out a huge laugh, right from the belly. She was incredibly apologetic and embarrassed, but the "pirate" couldn't care less. She checked out as fast as she could and pretty much ran out the door. I had a big smile on my face. I just got to talk to a real pirate, I thought.

She laughs about it now, but I can only imagine how flustered my mom was at the time.

I was 8 or 9 years old and the family was putting up hay one day. For the uninitiated, hay (or straw) is raised in a field, cut, raked, baled, and then collected. Steps 2-3-4 are all fairly easy on a tractor, but collecting the hay to take to the bar is a vigorous task, especially when you're just a young lad.

My older cousin (10-11) and I were the basic grunts. We would walk behind the wagon and throw bales of hay up on the wagon to be stacked and loaded. We'd switch off to "rest" between loading and stacking. Stacking being the easier of the two chores.

After a particularly long day in the field, we finally got all the hay loaded and stacked in the barn and sat down to rest in the front yard of our grandfather's house. We were soaked to the bone with sweat and completely funkified.

All of the older men and women in the family drank water or beer too cool off, but my cousin and I finished off our gallon of water and had nothing left. In an unprecedented, and henceforth never duplicated event, grandad gave me and my cousin a pony bottle of Rolling Rock beer to share. If you're not familiar with the brand, they used to make 7 oz. bottles of beer way back in the day. They called them "pony bottles", because there's a horse on the label and ponies are little horses. They still might make them for all I know.

Just being able to be 'one of the guys' after a long day of work and tossing back a beer was the ultimate "one of us" moments in my life. It's still the best beer I've ever had in my life. I've had better tasting beer, but there's no other singular beer experience that I've had that tops that one.
